text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's president Petar Stoyanov said he was dissolving parliament from February 19 and general elections would be held on April 19.
-- Sofia's mayor was sworn in to head a caretaker cabinet until after parliamentary elections in April. @

-- Bulgaria's parliament is expected to approve today amendments to the electoral law and to delegate extended powers to the interim cabinet to negotiate and receive loans from international financial institutions.

-- Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftohim said it had cut down daily fuel deliveries to local retailers to 680 tonnes of petrol and 680 tonnes of diesel. Neftohim used to deliver daily around 2,500 tonnes of petrol to fuel stations around the country. @
-- Bulgaria's parliamentary budget committee approved amendments to the income tax law, raising the untaxable mimimum income to 25,000 levs from 3,500 levs.
-- Bulgarian Brady bonds with a total par value of $133 million were used as means of payment in privatisation deals by November 30, the finance ministry said. @

-- Bulgaria's domestic debt rose to 1.678 trillion levs at the end of January from 1.053 trillion a month earlier because of the slump of the lev against the dollar and new government securities issued to finance the budget gap, the finance ministry said.

-- Bulgaria's state carrier Balkan Airlines board postponed by 24 hours all 16 outgoing Balkan flights on Wednesday because of protest action by technical staff demanding higher wages, Balkan's executive director Valeri Doganov said.
-- Sofia policemen protested in front of the presidency and the parliament demanding that their monthly salaries should be raised to the lev equivalent of $100 from current 28,000 levs.

-- Bulgaria's Chief Prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev said the prosecution would investigate reportedly illegal exports of millions of dollars by local commercial banks in recent months. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
